subject: Request: SKU exception + temporary billing hold for Stairwell AI Reserved Capacity
messages:
From: Arman Razi <arman@stairwell.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@stairwell.ai
Date: Sun, 5 Nov 2028 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Reserved capacity - special accelerator request (Stairwell)

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have an internal ask from infra: because of a latency-sensitive model path, we need guaranteed access to a specific H200x variant (not the default H200S) for 12 months. Our procurement team is asking whether Redwood can: 1) reserve a fixed pool of H200x for Stairwell (16 GPUs) with a temporary pricing hold for the first 3 months while we ramp, and 2) allow a one-time short burst of +50% capacity at the H200x SKU during our Q1 launch week without the usual overage surcharge.

I attached a short provisioning request and a sample usage file. Can you confirm if this SKU can be reserved, and whether you can provide a short-term billing hold / reduced overage for the initial ramp? If there are contract redlines required for the non-standard SKU and burst carveout, please point me to the right folks.

Best,
Arman
Co-founder, Stairwell AI

Attachments: stairwell_provisioning_request.pdf, estimated-usage-samples.csv

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Nov 2028 19:02:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Reserved capacity - special accelerator request (Stairwell)

Looping you both in — Stairwell (DEAL-7832) is asking for three non-standard asks: dedicated H200x SKU assignment, a 3-month billing hold / capped overage for ramp, and one-time +50% burst at the same SKU without standard surcharge. They say the burst is critical for their launch.

Quick thoughts:
- H200x availability: engineering says H200x is supported in Dedicated but it’s a limited family in us-west; we’d need an explicit SKU carveout in the reservation.
- Billing hold: finance can allow a temporary rate-limited hold but needs exec signoff for waived overage risk.
- Burst exemption: this is the contentious item; we can do a hard-coded burst window with a cap but removing surcharge entirely will need a compensation trade (e.g., higher monthly commitment or a one-time commercial credit).

Can one of you draft the commercial ask (terms + recommended concession) so I can escalate to Aditya for approval? I can share the procurement doc and usage samples.

-Rishi
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Nov 2028 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity - special accelerator request (Stairwell)

Thanks Rishi — drafting recommended terms below for escalation.

Proposed commercial package (to present to Aditya for signoff):
- SKU carveout: Reserve 16x H200x (dedicated pool) for 12 months. Customer commits to a 12-month reserved contract with a 55% uplift vs hosted list price (covers higher SKU premium).
- Ramp billing hold: For months 1-3, cap monthly spend at 60% of forecasted committed spend (per their attached CSV). Any usage above the cap will be deferred to month 4 and amortized at the committed rate (no surcharge). This is a temporary accounting/hold; terms must be explicit in term sheet.
- Burst window: Allow a single 7-day burst window (client-controlled) up to +50% additional H200x capacity. Overage pricing for that window: apply a reduced surcharge (25% of standard overage rate) rather than full surcharge.
- Trade: Customer accepts a one-time setup/engineering fee of $120k and a 5% increase to the committed monthly baseline for months 4-12.

Risks / notes: engineering needs a hard lead-time of 6 weeks to bake the SKU placement. If Aditya won't sign off on reduced burst surcharge, propose replacing it with a larger one-time credit and/or higher committed baseline.

I’ll prepare a redline to the term sheet (attaching redwood-term-sheet-v3.docx) and can go to legal. If agreed, Rishi — can you ask Stairwell to confirm the requested 7-day window timing (they mentioned "Q1 launch week")?

-Lauren
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-term-sheet-v3.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Nov 2028 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity - special accelerator request (Stairwell)

I like the structure. A couple of technical/commercial clarifications to include before we ping Aditya: 
- Preemption protection: Stairwell is asking for consistent H200x placement. We can mark the reservation as "preferred" on specific racks to reduce preemption risk, but full non-preemptible SLA is a material product change; if they need non-preemptible guarantees, that requires an SLA amendment and should be priced accordingly.
- Burst implementation: the +50% burst will require a temporary reservation hold across adjacent availability zones; that increases our scheduling risk for other customers. Recommend adding a contingent clause: if adjacent AZs cannot supply the exact H200x variant during the burst, fallback to H200S at the same reduced surcharge.
- Finance ask: recommend the one-time engineering fee be invoiced on contract signing and credited against month 3 if ramp targets are hit.

If everyone agrees, I suggest Rishi does a concise one-pager for Aditya with these ask bullets and the trade. I can add the technical fallback language.

-Karthik
Head of Product, Dedicated Platforms

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Nov 2028 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity - special accelerator request (Stairwell)

Thanks team — reviewed the package. Approve on the following conditions: 
1) Customer signs the 12-month reservation at the proposed uplift and the one-time engineering fee is non-refundable but credited against month 3 if ramp targets are met (as Karthik suggested).
2) Burst window: approve a single 7-day +50% burst with reduced surcharge (25% of standard) subject to fallback to H200S if exact variant availability fails. Explicitly include language that the burst is a best-effort carveout; no SLA for burst fulfillment.
3) Legal to add clause that the H200x SKU assignment is "preferred placement" and that full non-preemptible guarantees are out-of-scope for this contract. If Stairwell requires non-preemptible, we will price separately.
4) Finance to confirm the temporary billing hold mechanics; operationally we will cap months 1-3 as Lauren proposed, and deferred billings will be amortized starting month 4.

Rishi — escalate to legal and finance with these bullets and attach the redlined term sheet. Once legal signs off, coordinate signature with Stairwell (DocuSign link attached above).

-Aditya
COO, Redwood Inference
